title: Read: blocks
description: Which blocks one world carries, each one's declared version and its encoded size. Answered by POST /world/blocks (Sim/icarus_sim/terrain_read.blocks_request). A read document, never a world and never a handle: reads produce no version. The read documents are schema'd rather than the blocks they describe - seven of the 49 blocks in terrain_history.STATE_KEYS have a schema file of their own and the rest reach world-output.schema.json as a declared property, which board/backlog/PRODUCT-BLOCK-REGISTRY.md owns and this boundary makes visible rather than fixes.

blocks.description: One row per top-level key the world carries, sorted by name - the order the transfer bytes are written in. Built by walking the world, never by walking the registry: a report derived from terrain_history.STATE_KEYS would omit a block the world carries and the registry does not, which is the materialize_stage failure mode docs/conformance/nomads.md documents.

total_bytes.description: Sum of every encodable block's bytes. Larger than what crosses to a host, because the transfer form also drops build_stages and every nested timing_ms.

unregistered.description: Keys this world carries that terrain_history.STATE_KEYS does not list. Not an error: config, layers, timing_ms, build_stages, generator_version, recipe, warnings and the per-call report blocks are all legitimately unregistered. A block that looks like state and appears here is the thing to look at.

absent.description: Registered blocks this world does not carry. world_clock and quests are absent from every world that has never been advanced.

unencodable.description: Blocks JSON cannot carry, which in practice means a non-finite float. A world holding one can never be named by a host, and naming the block is more use than failing the report.

source.description: Which world answered, read straight off the document. Not a handle: naming a world by its content is the host's job and stays on the far side of the boundary.

day.description: world_clock.day, or null on a world that has never been advanced.

registered.description: Listed in terrain_history.STATE_KEYS, so carried across an age boundary and snapshotted into build_stages.

version.description: block['version'], only where the block declares an integer one. Never inferred.

count.description: Members for an object or an array; null for a scalar.
